extracted.intended_audience: NIH review panel / program officers and institutional grant administrators; applicants preparing an F99/K00 Facilities & Other Resources section
extracted.subtask_description: The Facilities & Other Resources section of an NIH F99/K00 grant application describing cores, laboratory space, computing infrastructure, data systems, cohorts, equipment, and institutional certification/support. Intended to document available resources and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CLIA-certified laboratories for patient assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: The OADC Clinical Core uses the CLIA certified laboratories of the OHSU for patient assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates clinical samples are processed in CLIA-certified facilities suitable for patient testing and regulatory compliance; supports validity of clinical measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of MRI research systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The OHSU Department of Radiology supports one 1.5 T GE, and one 3 T Siemens MRI system utilized for research for the OADC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies on-campus MRI hardware available to the project; supports imaging protocol feasibility and scheduling for proposed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuropathology Core dedicated laboratory space and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Neuropathology Core consists of 3 rooms containing a total of 775 square feet including a full histology area with appropriate venting (room 1352), a biochemical workspace with biosafety cabinet (room 1358), and a workspace (room 1364) with desks and bench space; fixed and frozen brain tissues dissected in a dedicated 150 sq ft morgue alcove (room 2310-C); brain autopsies performed in the fully equipped OHSU Department of Pathology Richard Jones Hall Morgue, room 2310; dedicated storage space in room 2310 and 150 sq ft of room 1329 Richard Jones Hall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents specific lab spaces, biosafety equipment, dissection/autopsy facilities, and storage required for neuropathology tasks; supports capability to perform tissue processing and histology per proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomarkers Core laboratory and sample handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Biomarkers Core is assigned a 400 square foot laboratory; blood is collected in the clinical research unit and CSF and plasma divided and snap frozen prior to transfer; DNA is extracted from whole blood in the Biomarkers Core laboratory; lab equipped with centrifuge, pipetters, bench space, hood space, NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer; four -80 freezers for sample storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies sample collection, processing workflow, and essential equipment for biomarker assays; demonstrates capacity for biospecimen handling and molecular assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alarmed -80°C freezers for sample protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The freezers are all alarmed to permit rescue of the samples in the event of a power or equipment failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows sample security and continuity-of-storage measures (alarms) to prevent specimen loss and to meet good laboratory practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuroimaging Core capabilities and longitudinal database
rubrics_metrics.description: Neuroimaging Core supports in vivo 3T MRI acquisition and analysis, has an extensive longitudinal database of over 3700 MRIs from over 1000 subjects, has developed advanced imaging sequences and analysis techniques, 7T post-mortem imaging protocol, and collaborations enabling tau-PET imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates imaging expertise, existing data resources, and methodological capabilities relevant to proposed imaging aims and longitudinal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Imaging Research Center (AIRC) instrumentation and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: AIRC houses 3 research-dedicated MR instruments (whole-body Siemens TIM Trio 3T, whole-body Siemens 7T, small animal Bruker BioSpin 12T), administrative and preparation areas, image processing lab, chemistry lab, animal surgery, electronics/machine shop, home-built mock scanner, satellite pharmacy with DEA license, and a satellite 2500 ft2 facility with whole-body Siemens Trio 3T at the Oregon National Primate Research Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an inventory of high-end imaging instruments, supporting labs, and licensed pharmacy facilities indicating capacity for advanced in vivo and animal imaging studies and required ancillary services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology Group (ITG) support functions
rubrics_metrics.description: ITG develops, implements, and maintains technology-based solutions including maintaining the OHSU network and web system, computer and software upgrades, e-mail, computerized patient record systems, purchasing/installation program, technical help and training for researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents institutional IT support for research computing, data systems, and researcher training — relevant for implementation and maintenance of project systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Computing Center (ACC) service offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: ACC provides consulting, research storage solutions, secure local and remote collaboration options, virtual server environments (Windows and Unix), equipment hosting, application hosting and license management, co-location and support for research computing systems, and access to >100 open-source research applications and statistical/simulation packages; services available at nominal cost or modest fees for more complex needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes computing services and cost structure available to investigators for data processing, storage, and application hosting; supports feasibility of computational aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACC supported operating systems and virtualization
rubrics_metrics.description: The OHSU ACC currently runs Solaris, Mac OS X, RedHat and Ubuntu LTS Linux, and Windows; maintains a VMWare cluster and supports hosted customer compute clusters; designed to accommodate any required OS; collaborating with Intel on cloud cluster development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates flexible, multi-platform compute environment and virtualization infrastructure for custom research computing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network architecture to avoid bandwidth contention
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACC’s network infrastructure consists of four high-speed switches delivering Gigabit Ethernet to all hosted resources as well as a limited number of 10 Gigabit connections. This exclusively switched architecture was designed to eliminate the network bandwidth contention common in research environments, while allowing reliable high and low bandwidth connections between OHSU researchers, the Internet, and OHSU’s 10 Gigabit connection to Internet2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies network design and bandwidth provisions to support high-throughput data transfer and reliable connectivity for collaborative research and large datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tape backup system and backup schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACC’s tape backup system consists of a dedicated high-end server with multiple Gigabit network, SCSI and fiber channel interfaces; uses commercial-grade backup software controlling a tape library with overall capacity of approximately 120 terabytes; performs a full back-up every week and daily incremental backups; off-site tape rotation to a secure location keeps mission-critical data safe while maintaining compliance with OHSU data retention policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents backup architecture, capacities, backup cadence, and off-site rotation to support data integrity and institutional retention/compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACC authentication, confidentiality, encryption and security governance
rubrics_metrics.description: ACC customers authenticate against the OHSU Active Directory when possible; for external collaborators ACC staff create OHSU accounts or ACC-specific accounts; users must read and sign OHSU’s Confidentiality Statement and Network Services Usage Agreement; all ACC users are required to use encryption per OHSU policies and HIPAA guidelines; ACC facilitates encryption solutions and provides a Secure Remote Access Portal; ACC employs a secondary firewall, has been reviewed by the OHSU Office of Integrity, and undergoes periodic internal security audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details access control, legal/confidentiality agreements, encryption/HIPAA compliance, and institutional security oversight necessary for handling protected health information and secure research data.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACC staffing levels and support personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Core staffing for the Center is provided by six full-time Research System Engineers, two part-time System Analysts, and two part-time Database Analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates available technical personnel for system administration, user support, and data management to sustain project computing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical data center security controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Data centers require a check-in at a guard station and data center employee escort; employees must display badges; server racks require both a key and keycard to access; facilities have security cameras monitoring 24/7 and presence of OHSU Public Safety officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents physical access controls and monitoring protecting servers and research infrastructure, supporting data security and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-space computing and local backup practices
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel are provided personal computers; DMSC database server resides on an iMac (3.06 GHz Intel Core 2 Duo, 500 GB, 8 GB RAM); incremental database backups to a password protected computer are performed each workday and are also copied to the OHSU ACC; facility maintains daily incremental tape backups and an 800 GB secure drive with one-month retention including a weekly tape copy stored offsite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes desktop/server specs, routine incremental backups, and off-site redundancy to ensure local data resilience and alignment with central backup infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office space allocation for Center activities
rubrics_metrics.description: About 2,000 square feet of modern contiguous dedicated research space is allotted for the OADC in the Hatfield Research Building, including a 20-person conference room dedicated for OADC use; additional 500 square feet of cubicle space in the Center for Health & Healing 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates availability of contiguous office and meeting space for administrative, collaborative, and training activities described in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical examination space and participant visit flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Aging & Alzheimer’s Clinic patients are examined in the Platinum LEED certified Center for Health and Healing; non-cognitively impaired community subjects are assessed in OCTRI outpatient units staffed by RNs and research assistants (11 exam rooms, procedure rooms, phlebotomy space); participants are also seen in their homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents access to appropriate clinical exam rooms and capacity for home-based visits, supporting proposed participant assessments and recruitment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offsite community-based study space and home visit infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical evaluations for ORCATECH site are performed at continuous care retirement centers, retirement homes, subsidized housing venues, community centers and participants’ homes; participating retirement communities may provide conference rooms for examination and testing; most research visits are completed as individual home visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates logistical availability for community-based data collection and home-based evaluation protocols relevant to proposed community cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCATECH Life Laboratory (OLL) in-home sensor platform and cohort
rubrics_metrics.description: OLL is a community-based resource of volunteer seniors allowing technologies deployed and tested in their homes; as of December 2017 OLL has 128 active participants (about 110 homes), semi-annual cognitive and neurological batteries, weekly reports of health and life events; deployed technologies include activity sensors, contact sensors, phone sensors, home computers, medication tracking devices, bio-impedance scale, temperature and CO2 sensors; longitudinal database of continuous activity data and weekly online reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes an existing in-home sensor cohort and instrumentation platform to test devices and algorithms in real-world settings prior to larger deployments — useful for validation and pilot studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCATECH Information System architecture and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: A sophisticated big data repository/configuration manager storing data within relational and non-relational databases on 1 and 10 Gbe networks and raw binary repositories; back-end server farm includes web server, cluster of 5 Apache Kafka nodes and 5 Xen servers hosting 16 VMs for web requests, DNS, VPN, email, builds/version control, backup, management, graph DB and Spark interfaces; isolated 1 Gb network with 7 Apache Cassandra/Spark nodes for long-term storage/analysis; backend MySQL database runs on a 24-core 3.3 GHz machine with 64 GB RAM; system has handled receipt/storage of 3 MB of data per home daily for up to 300 homes and is linearly scalable through additional nodes; storage includes 26 TB SAN and iSCSI tape backup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides detailed software/hardware stack and measured throughput/scale demonstrating capacity to collect, store, and analyze sensor and subject-generated data at scale for the proposed program.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCATECH Management Console for cohort/system oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: An online database interface used to manage ORCATECH cohorts (over 500 subjects) allowing secure remote management of cohorts, tracking adherence to questionnaires (including weekly questionnaires), tracking upcoming in-person clinical evaluations, tracking health issues, and managing in-home systems (inventory, sensor 'health', data reliability, remote fixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes tools for remote monitoring and operational management of deployed homes and cohort engagement, supporting study operations and data quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment Development Lab prototyping resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A 200 square-foot room equipped with electronic test equipment and stock of components for prototype design including digital and analog oscilloscopes, signal generators, digital counters and voltmeters, spectrum analyzer, power supplies, engineering work stations for circuit board layout, PSpice, PIC microcontroller firmware development, optical breadboards, mounts and components, and hand tools for prototype fabrication and small production runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents local capacity for hardware prototyping, testing, and small-scale production to support device development and modifications required by research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of equipment needs (none major required)
rubrics_metrics.description: No major items of equipment will be used in the activities proposed in this application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares that the project does not require acquisition of major new equipment, which affects budget and institutional support considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formatting requirement and maximum page length for NIH biosketches; noncompliance may lead to administrative issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional certification of candidate eligibility and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter certifies the candidate (Ms. Yu) has passed qualifying exam and advanced to candidacy, has completed all requirements except dissertation, and that USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work’s facilities and environment will provide necessary support, multidisciplinary environment, mentoring, library and IT resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates institutional commitment and candidate eligibility required for the F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research Award; supports training environment adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Number: 4040-0010 Expiration Date: 12/31/2022; OMB No. 0925-0001 and 0925-0002 (Rev. 03/2020) and tracking number GRANT13232827; Funding Opportunity Number: RFA-AG-21-022; Received Date timestamps present.
